summary: Describes how EAP-FAST can carry a basic password exchange based on the Generic Token Card method (EAP-GTC). The password is sent inside a TLS-protected tunnel that mutually authenticates the peer and server. This is an informational document.

eli5.summary: First you build a safe tube between two computers. Then you send the password through the tube, so nobody on the outside can see it.

questions: how does eap-fast send a password
why can eap-gtc not be used inside eap-fast
what are the eap-fast gtc error codes
subtitle: How a plain username and password are carried safely inside the EAP-FAST encrypted tunnel.

tldr.problem: Networks with legacy user databases, password changes and one-time-password features need a way to check a user's password during EAP-FAST authentication.
tldr.mechanism: EAP-FAST-GTC runs inside the TLS tunnel set up by EAP-FAST. The server sends a CHALLENGE, the peer replies with RESPONSE holding username and password, and failures are reported with an E= packet carrying a numeric error code.
tldr.outcome: It documents existing practice for interoperability. It reuses EAP Type 6, which the IESG note says is incompatible with EAP method negotiation, so it must stay inside the tunnel.

today: RFC 5421 is an Informational RFC (March 2009), and the unit metadata shows no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. The IESG note says it documents current use of existing EAP methods within EAP-FAST to promote interoperability.

sections.title: What EAP-FAST-GTC Is
sections.content:
EAP-FAST mutually authenticates a peer and a server using a TLS tunnel. This RFC describes its inner method EAP-FAST-GTC, which authenticates the peer with a basic password exchange. It was developed to support cleartext passwords against legacy user databases, to make password changes possible, and to support one-time-password features such as new pin mode.

The messages are cleartext strings, but they travel inside the encrypted TLS tunnel and are therefore considered secure. The method reuses EAP Type 6, originally given to EAP-GTC, but its payloads need specific formatting. So EAP-FAST-GTC MUST NOT be used outside an EAP-FAST tunnel, and EAP-GTC MUST NOT be used inside one. All packets are carried in EAP Payload TLVs.
sections.eli5: It is a way to send a password through a locked tube. The password itself is written in plain words, but nobody can read it inside the tube.

sections.title: The Message Format
sections.content:
Every packet except the empty acknowledgment uses a LABEL=Value format. Labels are ASCII and contain no spaces. Three are defined: CHALLENGE from the server (for example a prompt to enter the password), RESPONSE from the peer, and E for a server failure. A packet in any other format SHOULD make the receiver fail authentication with a failure Result TLV.

After the tunnel is up and phase 2 starts, the server sends a challenge. The peer may prompt the user or use credentials it already has. It replies with RESPONSE=user@example.com\0secret, where a NULL character separates the username from the password. Sending both together in the first response saves the inner EAP-Identity round trip.

The server SHOULD first check the user identity against the Initiator ID in the PAC-Opaque (RFC 5422) and, if it matches, authenticate the user against its internal or external databases. More exchanges may follow, for instance a request for the next token or a new pin. The exchange ends when a Result TLV arrives.
sections.eli5: The server asks a question, the computer answers with a name and a password, and they can go back and forth until the server says yes or no.

sections.title: Failure Packets and Error Codes
sections.content:
A failure is sent as E=eeeeeeeeee R=r M=<msg>. The first part is a decimal error code, the R flag is 1 if a retry is allowed and 0 if not, and the message is human-readable ASCII. Peers SHOULD handle unknown codes gracefully and ignore unknown label/value pairs.

With the retry flag set to 1 the server disables short timeouts and expects the peer to prompt for new credentials. With 0, the peer SHOULD NOT prompt again without restarting EAP-FAST from the beginning. An unrecoverable failure is acknowledged with an empty EAP-FAST-GTC packet, and the server can send the error code together with the Result TLV for protected termination, so no extra round trips are needed.

The format is similar to MSCHAPv2 errors, minus the server challenge. Non-ASCII usernames, passwords and messages may be sent as UTF-8, processed as in RFC 4282 and RFC 5198.
sections.eli5: If the answer is wrong, the server sends back a number that says why, like a locked account or an old password, and whether you may try again.

sections.title: Security Rules and Claims
sections.content:
Because passwords are sent in the clear, the method MUST NOT be used outside a protected tunnel with strong protection. Weak encryption such as 40-bit or the NULL cipher MUST NOT be used. The peer MUST authenticate the server before disclosing credentials, so EAP-FAST-GTC MUST NOT be the inner method in Server-Unauthenticated Provisioning Mode. It MAY be used in normal EAP-FAST authentication and in Server-Authenticated Provisioning Mode.

The server needs the actual secret, so the RFC recommends varying the stored validation data by domain, so that one compromised server does not compromise others. The method generates no session keys, so the MSKi used for EAP-FAST crypto-binding is all zeros. The security claims table says it has no dictionary attack protection of its own, but the TLS tunnel prevents an off-line dictionary attack. Credentials used here SHOULD NOT be used in other unprotected mechanisms.
sections.eli5: Never send the password unless the tube is strong and you are sure who is at the other end. Otherwise someone could read it.

sections.title: IANA Registry
sections.content: EAP-FAST-GTC uses the already assigned EAP Type value 6. The RFC creates a registry named "EAP-FAST GTC Error Codes", assigned by Specification Required, and lists seven initial codes. No registry is created for Labels, as implementations support only the ones defined here and new ones are not expected.
sections.eli5: The error numbers go on an official list so everyone uses the same meanings.

items.label: ERROR_RESTRICTED_LOGON_HOURS
items.desc: Access attempted outside the allowed hours.

items.label: ERROR_PASSWD_EXPIRED
items.desc: Password expired; a change is required.

items.label: ERROR_NO_DIALIN_PERMISSION
items.desc: Access denied for lack of dial-in permission.

items.label: ERROR_CHANGING_PASSWORD
items.desc: Password change failed, likely a complexity policy.

items.label: ERROR_PAC_I-ID_NO_MATCH
items.desc: The PAC cannot be used for this user account.
